task.description: WF-03 Step 3d -- REVIEWER hard gate on implementation commit bcddcebf (handoff 317fcc75), the ISS-0765 fix correcting web/src/api/identity.ts's groupsApi off the dead /api/v1/admin/groups/ prefix. Primary question: does the implementation match the gated design (lib/letflow/design/iss-0765-groupsapi-route-prefix-audit.md, commit 1fca1613, PASSED by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR on rework 1) exactly -- no more and no less? Check both directions: design decisions not implemented, and changes made the design does not authorise. Charter scope is idiom, scope creep and decision-record consistency; the OTP/supervision half is expected to be inapplicable since nothing under lib/ changed, and REVIEWER should say so rather than stretch it. Scope creep is the main risk: six adjacent defects found during this run are deliberately OUT of scope and already filed separately as ISS-0811, ISS-0812, ISS-0813, ISS-0814, ISS-0815 and ISS-0816. FRONTEND-DEV reports type-check, lint, 874 tests and 48 guards all green, and states plainly it could NOT verify against a live backend (no listener on localhost:4000) -- static green is not integration evidence and the gap must be noted in the verdict, not silently accepted.
acceptance_criteria: Every diff hunk traces to a design section authorising it, and every design decision (a)-(d) is implemented.

No out-of-scope change: Group.is_system/member_count (ISS-0811), usersApi/rolesApi routes (ISS-0812), User.status casing (ISS-0814), User.roles/created_at (ISS-0815), CursorPage<T>.has_more and the members dialog's 50-row truncation (ISS-0816) are all absent from the diff.
INV-C holds: web/src/api/__tests__/identity.removeMembers.test.ts and the removeMembers call are byte-unchanged.
Exactly the seven enumerated GroupsPage.tsx edits, no eighth, with :108's dependency array textually unchanged.
The useMemo added after :58 is a consumer-side convenience over an already-correctly-typed value, NOT the normalising shim decision (b) forbids per docs/guides/frontend_developer_guide.md:83-88.
The comment replacing .get/.update records them as unimplemented backend-side (AC3's second disjunct), not as a TODO to re-add.
Decision (c) restores rather than contradicts the premise recorded at lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:483-489.
GroupMember's status/auth_source unions are lowercase, matching what user_map/1 actually emits -- the new code must not repeat the ISS-0814 mistake.
The absence of integration evidence is recorded in the verdict as a condition on Step 5, not treated as closed.

summary.verdict: PASS -- implementation matches the gated design in both directions
summary.one_line: Every design decision (a)-(d) is implemented, nothing beyond them is, all four new interfaces were re-derived field-for-field from the live backend source rather than inherited from the design, and the seven GroupsPage.tsx edits are exactly the enumerated set with no eighth.
summary.charter_applicability: The OTP/supervision half of the REVIEWER charter is INAPPLICABLE to this diff and was not stretched to fit. Nothing under lib/ changed, no gen_statem callback, supervision tree or process lifecycle is touched, and Letflow.InstanceSupervisor is not in the blast radius. Charter items 1 (gen_statem idiom) and 2 (supervision isolation) are recorded as N/A. Items 3 (type-safety) and 4 (scope creep), plus decision-record consistency, are the live half and are where this gate's work went.

shim_question_decision_b.verdict: NOT A SHIM -- consumer-side convenience over an already-truthful value. Decision (b) is honoured.
reasoning: The prohibition in docs/guides/frontend_developer_guide.md:83-88 is specifically against normalising a MISMATCH: 'If web/ expects a field, a status code, or a pagination cursor that Letflow's API doesn't produce ... do not add a shim or adapter inside web/ that normalises the mismatch.' Here there is no mismatch left to normalise -- GroupMemberPage is a field-for-field transcription of what the server actually emits, verified against source below.

The useMemo invents no field, renames no field, and supplies no default for any wire value. It selects .items, which the server does produce, and substitutes [] only for React Query's undefined -- the query is created with enabled: Boolean(activeGroup), so undefined is a client-side not-yet-fetched state, not a server response. Defaulting a loading state is not defaulting a wire shape.

Nothing is discarded or hidden. membersPage stays in scope at the call site with next_cursor and count intact and reachable -- which is exactly the visibility decision (b) rationale 3 was protecting. An unwrap inside groupsApi.members would have destroyed them for every future consumer including the mobile tier; this does not.
INV-B scopes the prohibition to web/src/api/. The derivation lives in the page component, one layer below the contract boundary, and is invisible to any other client.

The compiler-as-detector property that decision (b) rationale 2 was bought for is intact: any OTHER consumer of groupsApi.members would still receive GroupMemberPage and still be a type error if it treated the value as an array. The useMemo narrows one call site's local binding, it does not weaken the exported type.
shim_question_decision_b.counterfactual_that_would_have_failed: Had the same expression been written inside groupsApi.members -- client.get<GroupMemberPage>(...).then(r => r.items) -- that WOULD be the forbidden shim: the declared return type would no longer be the wire body, next_cursor would be unreachable from every consumer, and INV-B would break. It is not what was written.

The contrast is instructive rather than harmful today, but it is the second place in this file where User's optional-everything shape forces a defensive fallback. Worth watching when ISS-0812/0815 give usersApi its own pass -- the right end state is that the User-side fallback disappears the same way the members-side one just did.

integration_evidence_gap.severity: RECORDED, NOT BLOCKING at this gate
integration_evidence_gap.statement: Static green is NOT integration evidence and is not counted as such here. Every command above type-checks, lints or exercises the code against a vi.fn() spy whose Response the test itself constructs -- no HTTP request leaves the process and no Letflow instance was dialled. FRONTEND-DEV's own report states plainly that a probe of http://localhost:4000/api/v1/identity/groups got no connection (HTTP 000), and that statement is accepted as honest rather than claimed away.
integration_evidence_gap.what_is_therefore_unproven: That /api/v1/identity/groups, /api/v1/identity/groups/:id, /api/v1/identity/groups/:id/members and the { user_id } add-member body actually return 2xx against a running server with a real :GroupsManage-bearing token. The route table was read from source and the six routes demonstrably exist, so the prefix correction is sound BY CONSTRUCTION -- but construction is not execution. The specific thing no test in this run can catch is a discrepancy between the route macros as written and the pipeline as actually mounted at runtime.
integration_evidence_gap.who_owns_closing_it: UAT-RUNNER, once an instance is up. Scope: list groups, open Manage members, add a member, remove a member, delete an empty group -- the scope FRONTEND-DEV itself nominated, which I endorse. This gap must be carried into the run's closing handoff so Step 5 does not close ISS-0765 claiming end-to-end evidence it does not have.

design_artefact_observations.consequence: If a later step audits the implementation against the design's HEADER counts rather than its tables, it will report a spurious mismatch. It should not.
